sections.body:

sections.body: Ship sections and equipment may be heavy, have designated lifting points, or be easily damaged. Follow site procedures for rigging plans, inspected equipment, capacity, communication, exclusion zones, and weather conditions. Protect surfaces and components during storage.
sections.title: Concepts and Limits of This Material

sections.body:
Check weight and lifting-point marks and the approved plan. Do not enter beneath a suspended load or direct the operation unless designated. Secure components on suitable supports and protect them from water, corrosion, and impact.

Practice scenario: A component is suspended, and a worker asks you to pass underneath it to get a tool.
Response: Do not pass underneath; wait until the load is placed safely and use an approved alternative route.

lessons.caution: Do not remove a lock or tag or change system status just to close a shift record.

checks.explanation: Accurate information prevents another team from entering work that is not yet safe.
options: The location or system, results, isolation status, and work on hold
Only the list of completed work
The panel code without its status
A verbal note without the area identity

checks.explanation: Only authorized personnel may change an isolation, following the applicable procedure.
options: Keep the label in place and hand the status over to authorized staff
Remove the isolation because you have finished
Leave the label as it is without telling anyone
Ask an unassigned staff member to remove it

sections.body: Ship work passes between structural, machinery, outfitting, electrical, and inspection teams. Handovers identify the ship and area, system, revision, inspection results, energy and isolation status, work on hold, and access limits. Records must reflect the facts so the next team does not rely on assumptions.
sections.title: Concepts and Limits of This Material

sections.body:
Make sure area labels and status match the records. Directly communicate safety issues, items not yet released, and permits still in effect. Ask the recipient to repeat critical information. Update records through the official procedure.

Practice scenario: Your shift ends while the panel is still isolated and the work is unfinished.
Response: Keep the isolation label in place according to procedure and hand over the status to an authorized successor.
